identity.title: Unexpectedly large mass loss during the thermal pulse cycle of the red giant star R Sculptoris

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we report observations of CO emission from the circumstellar envelope and shell around R Sculptoris with an angular resolution of 1.3”.

question.value: What are the timescales and mass-loss properties during and after a thermal pulse of the AGB star R Sculptoris, as revealed by the CO(3-2) detached shell and spiral structure?

evidence.quote: It has hitherto been impossible to constrain observationally the timescales and mass-loss properties during and after a thermal pulse
The detached shell around R Sculptoris was observed in CO( _J_ = 3 − 2) emission at 345 GHz using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) during Cycle 0 operations
observed in CO( _J_ = 3 − 2) emission at 345 GHz
using the ALMA Cycle 0 compact configuration specifications
with an angular resolution of 1.3”

what.value: Present-day expansion velocity and mass-loss rate (3e-7 Msun/yr) of R Scl wind

evidence.quote: The present-day mass-loss rate is estimated to be 3×10 [−] [7] M `!` yr [−] [1] [,] [3]

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Modified GADGET-2 SPH models of the binary wind with radiative cooling, post-processed with LIME and CASA simdata

evidence.quote: we modeled the system with a modified version of the GADGET-2 SPH code [14], including detailed radiative cooling [15] .

unstated_but_needed: Calibration and imaging procedures (CASA version, weighting, cleaning), in supplementary information not provided
SPH model parameters (masses, separation, particle numbers)
Gas-mass and CO abundance assumptions for mass-loss rates

analysis_steps.goal: trace spiral in position angle vs radius

method.value: Linear fits to emission peaks in p.a. vs radius diagram of the systemic-velocity image, converted to wind velocity evolution assuming 350 yr orbital period

evidence.quote: The linear fits can hence be translated directly into a velocity evolution (Fig. 3).

assumptions.value: Orbital period 350 yr from present-day expansion velocity 10.5 km/s

evidence.quote: The present-day expansion velocity is estimated to be 10.5 km s [!1], giving a binary period of 350 years.

method.value: SPH binary wind model with derived velocity and mass-loss profiles as input, LIME radiative transfer, simdata, compared to observed image

evidence.quote: The modeled density, temperature, and velocity structures of the SPH model are then used as input in the 3-dimensional radiative transfer code LIME [16] .
The inclination angle of the binary system to the line of sight is 90 [o] .

validation.value: Model brightness distribution compared visually with observed intensities

evidence.quote: the brightness distribution reproduces the observed intensities well (Fig. 4)

used_for.value: SPH modelling of the binary wind

evidence.quote: modified version of the GADGET-2 SPH code [14]

used_for.value: 3D radiative transfer of the SPH model

evidence.quote: 3-dimensional radiative transfer code LIME [16]

used_for.value: simdata to simulate ALMA observations of the model

evidence.quote: processed by _simdata_ in _CASA_
shell radius of _R_ sh = 18.5”
shell expansion velocity of _v_ sh = 14.3 km s [−] [1]
constant separation of 2.6”±0.07”
giving a binary period of 350 years
An estimated total gas-mass in the shell of 2.5×10 [−] [3] M `!`

findings_qualitative.value: Spiral structure connects the central star to the detached shell, implying a binary companion

evidence.quote: we conclude that R Sculptoris is a binary system that underwent a thermal pulse ≈ 1800 years ago, lasting ≈ 200 years.

claims.hypothesis: Does R Scl host a binary companion that shapes the wind?
claims.experiment: ALMA CO(3-2) imaging plus SPH and LIME modelling
claims.result: Spiral of ~5 windings with spacing 2.6" reproduced by the binary SPH model
claims.finding: R Scl is a binary that had a thermal pulse ~1800 yr ago lasting ~200 yr

evidence.quote: we conclude that R Sculptoris is a binary system that underwent a thermal pulse ≈ 1800 years ago, lasting ≈ 200 years.

claims.hypothesis: How much mass is lost during the pulse?
claims.experiment: Shell mass and CO intensity ratios, SPH modelling
claims.result: Pulse mass-loss rate 7e-6 to 2.5e-5 Msun/yr, ~30 times the pre-pulse rate
claims.finding: About 3 times more mass is returned to the ISM than previously thought

evidence.quote: This shows that ≈ 3 times more mass is returned to the interstellar medium during and immediately after a pulse than previously thought.

limitations_admitted.value: Intensity contrast between spiral windings and interwinding material indicates a more complicated mass-loss-rate variation than modelled

evidence.quote: variations in the intensity contrast between the spiral windings and interwinding material indicate a more complicated mass-loss-rate variation.

referee_caveats_inferred: Model is not uniquely fitted, no formal parameter search or uncertainties
Mass-loss rates depend on unstated CO abundance and distance

missing_for_reproduction: Supplementary information with data reduction and model details
reproducibility.score_reason: Data are public, but the main text omits reduction and modelling details.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Key recipe details are in unavailable supplementary information and the results rely on custom SPH modelling.

companion_papers.why: Present-day wind properties of R Scl
